(1) our PAS-based model outperforms word-sequence-based models on phrase similarity tasks, (2) our model is competitive with the previous best systems on these tasks, and (3) our model achieves these results without using pretrained word vectors or large training corpora.
we introduce a novel PAS-based language model, which is a simple and effective way of learning word representations and their compositions, and which outperforms previous wordsequence-based models.
we propose a novel PAS-based language model that jointly learns word representations, their composition functions, and the PASs themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing compositional models that learn word representations and their compositional functions from PASs.
developing a compositional language model based on predicate-argument structures that learns word representations and composition functions in an end-to-end manner.
developing compositional models that learn word representations and their compositional functions from predicate-argument structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model achieves the best performance on both phrase similarity datasets, and it is the only system to do so.
we have shown that our PAS model is competitive with the state of theart models on the phrase similarity task, and is able to achieve this performance without the need for pre-trained word vectors.
our PASbased language model achieves comparable results to state-of-theart word-sequence-based models while using much less training data and no pretrained word vectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that PASs can be effectively used in a compositional language model to learn better word representations.
we have developed a model which can be applied to any language, and that can learn the composition functions for the language from scratch.
our PAS-based model is able to learn better representations for words, predicates and arguments than the word-sequencebased model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PAS-based models can be used for word representations and that the PAS-based model can be used for learning word composition functions without the need of pretrained word vectors. 1
a compositional model can be learned using only bag-of-word contexts, and that PAS-based composition is more robust to noisy data than the sequencebased approach.
